faq.q: Why do I feel sad and excited about moving?
faq.a: Moving brings new things to look forward to, and it also means leaving people and places you love. Feeling both at once is normal and called mixed feelings.
asks: Is it normal to be upset about moving?

faq.q: How do I say goodbye to my friends?
faq.a: Spend time together before you go, swap addresses or numbers with a grown-up's help, take photos, or make each other a card. Plan a call for after the move.
asks: What should I do before I move away?

faq.q: How can I make a new place feel like home?
faq.a: Unpack your favourite things first, keep some routines the same, explore the area with your family, and join a club or activity to meet people.
asks: How do I settle into a new house?

faq.q: Can I stay friends with people after I move?
faq.a: Yes. Video calls, messages, letters and visits can keep friendships going, even across countries. Many friendships last for years after a move.
asks: Will my friends forget me when I move?

faq.q: What if I really do not want to move?
faq.a: Tell your family how you feel. The decision may not change, but sharing your worries helps them support you and plan things that make it easier.
asks: I do not want to move house

facts: On the well-known Holmes and Rahe stress scale from 1967, moving home is listed as one of the life events that cause stress.
About 281 million people, roughly 1 in 30 people worldwide, lived outside the country they were born in in 2020.
